title: Capacitor wafer bonded beneath transistor wafer at cell pitch
idea: Po: the capacitor lives in another factory. Etch ultra-deep trench capacitors (AR 100-150 in single-crystal Si, which does not lean like stacked pillars) on a cheap mature-node 'capacitor wafer', layer-transfer a thin single-crystal Si film on top at <400 C, then build access transistors with laser anneal and self-aligned contacts down to each buried capacitor.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): ~2x Cs from deeper single-crystal trenches; decouples capacitor and transistor thermal budgets and moves the capacitor module to an older, cheaper fab (capital, fact 4).

title: Transistorless crosspoint DRAM: threshold switch in series with capacitor
idea: Po: the array has no transistors. Each 4F2 crosspoint holds a MIM capacitor in series with an ovonic threshold switch that snaps on above ~1.5 V and is near-insulating below; half-select biasing writes and reads one cell, and the selector-capacitor pillar stacks in 4-8 decks like 3D XPoint but stores charge instead of phase.
why: Facts 2/4: 4F2 crosspoint with no lateral transistor sidesteps the 3D-DRAM transistor blocker; ~2 masks per deck gives ~3-5x bits per litho step. Risks: selector off-leakage sets retention and selector endurance must exceed 1e15.

title: Roll-to-roll oxide-TFT DRAM sheets laminated into thick stacks
idea: Po: memory is sold by the metre like tape. Sputter and nanoimprint oxide-TFT plus capacitor arrays roll-to-roll on 10 um polished metal foil at <300 C, then laminate 50-200 sheets with anisotropic conductive film and laser-drilled vertical bitline vias, the way multilayer ceramic capacitors stack 1000 layers.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4) and U.S. manufacturability: no EUV and no vacuum wafer fab for array layers; low per-layer density (F~100 nm) means it wins $/bit for capacity tiers, not latency.

title: Face-to-face mirror bonding shares sense amps across two arrays
idea: Po: two chips stare at each other in a mirror. Build identical array wafers with sense-amp stripes on alternate mats, flip one and hybrid-bond face to face so every sense amp senses a bitline from its own array against the mirrored twin bitline across the bond as the reference, the SA stripes interleaving like a zipper.
why: Periphery 49% (fact 7): sense-amp area per bit halves and the reference line has matched capacitance, cutting open-bitline noise; ~15-20% die area per bit saved.

title: Every vertical bitline bonded down to its own generous sense amp
idea: Po: the sense amp is bigger than the cells it serves. Fabricate only arrays on a litho-light 'array wafer' with vertical bitlines spanning 64+ tiers, and all sense amps and decoders on a separate logic wafer, hybrid-bonded at ~0.5 um pitch so each bond carries one vertical bitline to a large, low-offset sense amp.
why: Periphery 49% (fact 7) and capital: array fab drops logic-transistor steps (~30% fewer masks); larger matched sense amps (offset <5 mV) let Cs shrink, easing the charge wall.

title: Holes drilled in a bulk dielectric block form inter-hole capacitors
idea: Po: the capacitor is a hole, not a pillar. Deposit a 3-5 um block of crystalline high-k (rutile TiO2 or doped ZrO2, k 40-80), drill a hexagonal hole array, and fill alternate holes with storage and plate electrodes so the dielectric is the solid wall between neighbouring holes instead of a 5 nm conformal ALD film.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): reaches the k~70 target in a matrix that cannot lean or collapse; wall thickness set by etch spacing rather than ALD conformality at extreme AR.

title: Thousand-tier monolithic stack of atom-thin transistor sheets
idea: Po: tiers are counted in thousands, not tens. Grow wafer-scale MoS2 monolayers by MOCVD on sapphire, dry-stamp each 0.7 nm channel plus 3 nm high-k plus 5 nm metal as one 10 nm 'tier sheet', and pattern all tiers with one deep vertical-gate etch (3D NAND style) to get ~1000 lateral 1T1C tiers per 10 um of height.
why: Fact 2 (break-even at 26+ tiers): 1000 tiers at relaxed F~40 nm without EUV gives ~10x bits/cm2 of 2D DRAM; transfer yield per tier is the dominant risk.

title: Naturally layered crystal grows the 3D tier stack itself
idea: Po: chips are grown like minerals, not built. Epitaxially grow a Ruddlesden-Popper layered oxide whose unit cell alternates a semiconducting perovskite sheet with an insulating rock-salt spacer, so one PLD/MBE growth yields hundreds of perfectly registered channel/dielectric tiers; gate and bitline holes are then etched vertically through the crystal.
why: Fact 2: hundreds of superlattice deposition steps collapse into one epitaxy; atomically flat spacers give near-identical Vt in every tier.

title: Origami-folded membrane array stands planar capacitors on edge
idea: Po: memory is folded like a paper fan. Fabricate a 2D array with large, low-AR planar capacitors on a 50 nm membrane with stressed SiN/Cr bilayer hinges between cell rows; on release the membrane self-folds into a vertical accordion so each 0.1 um2 planar capacitor stands upright.
why: Charge wall and 3D blocker: ~20 fF planar capacitor in a ~0.005 um2 folded footprint, built flat with mature tools and no high-AR etch.

title: Block-copolymer gyroid sponge as a giant-area storage capacitor
idea: Po: the capacitor is a sponge. Self-assemble a block copolymer into a gyroid network over each access transistor, convert it to a porous metal scaffold with ~10 nm struts, island it per cell with a shallow trench, then ALD electrode/ZrO2/electrode inside for 20-40x projected area.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): area gain replaces the AR 60-75:1 pillar etch, the hardest step; bottom-up patterning removes one EUV layer.

title: Multi-fab tier sourcing: thin tier wafers from mature U.S. fabs
idea: Po: every tier comes from a different factory. Define an open 10 um-thin 'tier wafer' standard (array plus local sense, standard bond grid, redundancy lanes) that any 28-40 nm U.S. fab can make; a stacking house hybrid-bonds 8-32 known-good tiers from different suppliers onto a base logic die with per-tier remap.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: idle mature fab capacity produces DRAM bits; incremental capital is ~$50M stacking lines rather than $15B fabs.

title: Grounded shield tiers interleaved so no row has a neighbor
idea: Po: no row has a neighbour. In a stacked 3D DRAM, insert a grounded doped-Si or metal shield tier between active tiers and route wordlines so laterally adjacent cells belong to rows separated by a grounded wall; deposition tiers are cheap, so spending one tier in three on shielding buys electrostatic isolation.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): aggressor-victim coupling cut >10x, raising the threshold from ~1k toward 100k activations and removing mitigation refresh traffic.

title: Sixteen-cell micro-bitlines with per-tier oxide-TFT sense latches
idea: Po: every cell has a sense amp next door. In each oxide-semiconductor tier place a 4-TFT latch every 16 cells along the bitline so local bitline capacitance falls from ~60 fF to ~2 fF; latches drive a global bitline down to the base die.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): with Cb/Cs held at 2-4, Cs can be 0.5-1 fF and planar inside the tier, removing the tall capacitor that blocks 3D.

title: Uncut wafer-scale DRAM bonded onto wafer-scale compute
idea: Po: memory has no die edges. Keep the 300 mm DRAM wafer whole, stitch reticles with redundant cross-reticle wiring, map bad blocks at test, and bond it wafer-to-wafer onto a wafer-scale accelerator so every compute tile has its own DRAM directly above.
why: Data movement (fact 5) <0.3 pJ/bit vertically; no dicing, packaging or HBM TSV tax (fact 6); harvests every good block instead of scrapping dies.

title: Bond-interface dielectric turns facing pads into storage capacitors
idea: Po: the glue is the memory. Bond two wafers through a 4 nm ZrO2/Al2O3 laminate deposited on the facing Cu pads, so each pad pair becomes a MIM capacitor (~5-7 fF at 400 nm pitch); the top wafer holds access transistors and the bottom a common plate plus periphery.
why: Capital and U.S. manufacturability: a 28 nm-class fab gets DRAM with no capacitor module or high-AR etch at all, for low-cost capacity and embedded memory (larger cell, far cheaper flow).

title: Optical waveguide wordlines with photoconductive access devices
idea: Po: rows are opened by light. Replace metal wordlines with SiN waveguides over each row and use wide-bandgap photoconductors (ZnO or Ga2O3) as access devices that conduct only under a UV row pulse; transparent oxide tiers let one pulse address a vertical column of tiers.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): removes wordline CV2 (~30% of activation energy) and 3 V drivers; dark photoconductor leakage can be sub-fA.

title: Vertical bucket-brigade columns move charge to one sense amp
idea: Po: the bits move, the sense amp stays. Make each 3D column a vertical charge-coupled device whose tiers are three-phase clocked gate electrodes; charge packets shift down the pillar to a single sense amp at the bottom, with no per-cell access transistor or bitline contact.
why: Facts 2 and 7: no lateral transistor per cell and ~1 sense amp per 100+ bits; serial latency fits sequential AI weight streaming, not random access.

title: TSV-free memory stacks with inductive coupling between dies
idea: Po: the stack has no wires through it. Stack thinned DRAM dies with power fed by edge wraps and move data through on-die spiral coils at ~30 um pitch that couple inductively through 5-10 dies, placing coils over array area with no keep-out zones.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): reclaims TSV area and the 20-30% yield loss from TSV processing.

title: Chemically coded tier metals replace staircase contacts
idea: Po: the stack has no staircase. Build each tier's wordline from a distinct tungsten-free metal/liner pair (Mo, Ru, Co, TiN with unique etch-stop liners) so a contact etch stops on the target tier by chemistry; combined with binary chop etches, 64 tiers are contacted with ~6 masks in a single small contact field.
why: Facts 2/4: staircase area (~5-10% of die) and trim steps scale with tiers; chemical coding makes contact cost logarithmic and avoids tungsten (China ~80%).

title: Corrugated substrate hosts planar arrays on both sidewall faces
idea: Po: the wafer is not flat. Etch the silicon into 20:1 parallel walls before front-end processing, then build planar-transistor DRAM conformally on both wall faces with tilted implants and conformal ALD gates, so 1 cm2 of footprint carries ~10-20 cm2 of active surface.
why: Density without tier deposition: ~10x surface at relaxed F with no EUV; capacitors can run long along the wall.

title: Identical tiers self-number at power-up for stack-to-order capacity
idea: Po: tiers don't know who they are. Design every tier from one mask set with no tier-specific wiring; a daisy-chained token climbs the stack at power-up and each tier latches its address, so one assembly line builds 4- to 64-tier parts from the same wafers to match weekly demand.
why: Masks and capital: one mask set instead of per-tier variants; build-to-order capacity raises usable supply during shortages.

title: One transistor gates a string of resonance-staggered capacitors
idea: Po: one transistor, many capacitors. Above each vertical access transistor stack 4-8 capacitors, each behind a double-barrier resonant-tunnelling selector with a different resonance voltage set by well width, so the bitline bias chooses which single capacitor conducts: 1T-8C per footprint.
why: Density (fact 4): ~4-8x bits per transistor footprint without extra litho; risk is resonance selectivity and peak-to-valley ratio at room temperature.

title: Word-sized micro-mats, each with its own bond to logic
idea: Po: the page is the size of a word. Cut the array into 64x64-cell micro-mats, each with its own small sense amps and one sub-um hybrid bond straight down to the controller/compute die, so an activation opens only 64 bits and delivers all of them; millions of independent mats replace a few hundred 8 KB pages.
why: Overfetch (fact 8): 128x overfetch to ~1x, random-read energy from ~5.9 pJ toward <0.5 pJ per useful bit; also cuts data movement (fact 5).

title: Retention-graded tiers where data expires before it decays
idea: Po: memory that forgets on purpose. Build a 3D stack whose tiers are designed for graded, guaranteed retention (e.g., 50 ms, 2 s, 60 s via channel material and capacitor size), expose each tier's expiry in the address map, and have the allocator tag every buffer with a lifetime so activations, KV pages and gradients land in a tier that outlives them; refresh circuitry is omitted.
why: Refresh (fact 3): removes the ~46 fJ/bit refresh, 16-33% of idle power and 10-20% bandwidth loss, plus refresh logic area.

title: Ultra-wide-bandgap gallium-oxide vertical channels through every tier
idea: Po: the transistor is an insulator that occasionally conducts. Use ALD Ga2O3 (Eg ~4.8 eV, no hole conduction so no GIDL path) as a junctionless, fully depleted vertical access channel through each 3D tier; thermal generation scales as exp(-Eg/2kT), pushing off-current orders of magnitude below oxide channels like IGZO.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): <1e-20 A off-current gives hours of retention with ~2 fF at 85 C, so refresh never runs.

title: Loadless leakage-ratio latch stacked in oxide TFT tiers
idea: Po: the leak holds the bit instead of stealing it. Stack a 4-transistor loadless latch (n-type oxide drivers, p-type SnO or Te access-loads) in two monolithic tiers sized so p-load off-current exceeds n-driver off-current >10x; leakage itself pulls each node toward its stored state, so the cell is static and needs no refresh.
why: Refresh eliminated with ~10 aW standby per cell; two-tier stacking gives ~8-10F2 footprint, far denser than planar 6T SRAM, and fits BEOL above logic.

title: AI decode sweep doubles as free refresh by layout
idea: Po: the workload is the refresh controller. Stripe LLM weights so each token's matrix-vector pass activates every row of every bank and tier exactly once, guaranteeing a full sweep every 20-40 ms; row-open counters (already present for row-hammer tracking) certify coverage and the device issues zero refresh commands.
why: Refresh (fact 3): for inference memory, refresh energy and the 10-20% bandwidth tax drop to zero because activation already restores charge.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay access devices with literal vacuum gaps
idea: Po: the switch is a drawbridge that lifts away. Replace each tier's access transistor with a lateral NEM relay (5 nm-gap Ru cantilever pulled in by the wordline) so the off state is a physical gap with no subthreshold or junction leakage; retention is set only by capacitor dielectric leakage (hours to days).
why: Refresh eliminated; abrupt switching at ~0.5 V pull-in also attacks the voltage floor (fact 10). Risk: contact endurance must reach >1e15 cycles versus ~1e10-1e11 shown.

title: Buckled nanobeam bistable cells stacked in mechanical tiers
idea: Po: the bit is a shape, not a charge. Each cell is a pre-compressed 200 nm single-crystal Si nanobeam in a sealed cavity that buckles up or down; electrodes above and below snap it in ~10 ns and readout senses the capacitance difference, holding state with zero energy, and cavity tiers stack as bonded MEMS layers.
why: Zero refresh and standby; wear-free if strain stays elastic (<0.5% in single-crystal Si). Modest density aimed at a warm-data tier.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM stacks with superconducting cuprate power and wordlines
idea: Po: memory lives in a freezer. Immerse accelerator memory stacks in LN2 at 77 K where access leakage falls >1e6x and retention exceeds hours so refresh is disabled, and use YBCO or Bi-2223 global wordlines and power grids so tall stacks avoid IR drop; one cryostat per AI rack.
why: Refresh zero plus ~2x mobility; cryocooler overhead (~10 W per W removed) only pays off in dense AI racks.

title: Tunnel-FET access transistors in vertical 3D strings
idea: Po: the transistor opens only by quantum tunnelling. Make the vertical access device a heterojunction TFET (p+ SiGe source, intrinsic Si channel, n drain) with no thermionic subthreshold tail, giving aA-level off-current; its low on-current is acceptable because the 3D storage node is only ~1 fF.
why: Refresh eliminated by ~1e4x lower off-current than MOSFET tails; steep slope also lowers wordline voltage (fact 10).

title: Self-locking p-type cell with ground-idled bitlines
idea: Po: the stored bit locks its own door. Use a p-type oxide access transistor whose back-gate is the storage node itself, on an insulating substrate, and idle all bitlines at 0 V: a stored 0 sees no drain-source bias so it cannot leak, and a stored 1 raises its own back-gate and drives the channel deeper off.
why: Refresh: both states are self-protected by removing leakage drive instead of fighting the tail; retention limited by dielectric leakage (hours).

title: Let bits decay and recover them with cross-tier erasure codes
idea: Po: memory that is allowed to rot. Disable refresh and stripe each 64 B line across 12 tiers with an 8+4 Reed-Solomon erasure code plus weak-cell location maps from test, so the retention tail is corrected at read while the median cell holds data for minutes, longer than most working sets live.
why: Refresh zero by converting the leakage tail into a coding problem; 50% parity overhead is offset by cheap tiers and removed refresh periphery.

title: Bonded nonvolatile shadow tier dumps idle banks before power-off
idea: Po: memory that sleeps with its eyes shut. Pair each DRAM tier with a hybrid-bonded thick-oxide charge-trap shadow tier sharing its vertical bitlines, so an idle bank copies out in parallel in ~10 us and is power-gated; dumps are rate-limited to one per bank per 5 minutes, so 1e6-cycle endurance lasts ~10 years.
why: Refresh and idle power to zero for idle banks (16-33% of idle power, fact 3) without slowing active banks.

title: Redox-molecule monolayers in 3D capacitors hold charge for minutes
idea: Po: the capacitor is a molecule that refuses to give electrons back. Graft porphyrin or ferrocene redox monolayers inside porous 3D capacitor scaffolds so charge sits in discrete molecular oxidation states behind an activated electron-transfer barrier, giving minutes of retention without improving the access device.
why: Refresh skipped because retention exceeds data lifetimes; molecular charge density (~10-100 uC/cm2) also eases the charge wall (fact 1).

title: Factory-programmed charge-trap back-gates permanently stiffen every tier
idea: Po: the transistor is told once, forever, to stay off. Give each tier's lateral access transistors a buried ONO charge-trap back-gate programmed once at final test to shift Vt by about +0.8 V, cutting subthreshold leakage ~1e8x while a boosted front gate restores on-current; no negative wordline generator is needed.
why: Refresh: removes the subthreshold tail with one-time programming (no endurance concern) and trims tier-to-tier Vt spread; GIDL handled with a lightly doped drain.

title: Coulomb-blockade storage dots stacked in silicon nanowire tiers
idea: Po: the charge is too lonely to leave. Store each bit as a few electrons on a <3 nm Si dot whose charging energy (>10 kT at 300 K) blocks single-electron escape, coupled by direct tunnelling to a nanowire channel in each tier, with tiers formed from Si/SiGe superlattice nanowires.
why: Refresh: the blockade adds an energy barrier for second-to-hour retention while ns direct-tunnel writes avoid the oxide wear of flash.

title: Refresh-free device class written into standards and procurement
idea: Po: refresh is outlawed. Propose a JEDEC device class 'RF0' plus a CHIPS procurement preference: devices advertise per-region guaranteed retention, controllers carry data-expiry semantics (reads after expiry return poison), and refresh commands are optional, creating a market for long-retention 3D cells and lifetime-aware software.
why: Refresh power and bandwidth (fact 3) at system scale; policy pull for new U.S.-made cell types.

title: Sell retention-failed dies as never-refreshed ephemeral memory
idea: Po: the rejects are the product. Bin dies that fail the 64 ms retention spec but pass 4-8 ms and sell them as 'ephemeral memory' stacks for streaming workloads that must rewrite every buffer within a contractual window, enforced by a controller watchdog; refresh is never issued.
why: Supply: turns a top reject category into sellable bits (a few % more supply) at zero refresh power.

title: Witness cells per row enable decay-aware differential sensing
idea: Po: the bit knows how old it is. Store each row as differential 2T2C pairs inside the same vertical pillar so both halves leak almost equally (common mode), plus two witness cells written with known 1 and 0 at the same moment; at read the sense threshold is set from the witnesses, so data stays readable after 90% of the charge has leaked.
why: Refresh: retention becomes limited by leakage mismatch, not absolute leakage, ~10-30x longer (seconds), beyond activation and KV lifetimes.

title: Defect charge-state memory in stacked silicon-carbide sheets
idea: Po: the memory cell is a single missing atom. Store bits as the charge state of implanted point defects (e.g., divacancies in 4H-SiC) arrayed in thin bonded SiC sheets; a gate pulse moves the local Fermi level to set the charge state, which persists for days at room temperature because the level sits ~1 eV deep in the gap.
why: Zero refresh with wear-free switching (no atoms move); sensing through a nearby channel's conductance. Speed and density are speculative.

title: Breathing varactor capacitor stores at low voltage, reads boosted
idea: Po: the capacitor breathes. Replace the MIM capacitor with a MOS varactor whose plate line holds it in accumulation (high C) during idle so stored charge sits at ~0.2 V, then switches to depletion (C drops ~5x) at read to boost the node to ~1 V; at 0.2 V GIDL and junction leakage fall by orders of magnitude.
why: Refresh: idle leakage drive cut ~100x for tens of seconds retention, beyond working-set lifetimes; read gain also tolerates smaller Cs (fact 1).

title: Aging KV cache in never-refreshed tiers, models trained to forget
idea: Po: let memory forget like a brain. Store KV-cache and activation low-order bit-slices in never-refreshed tiers and sign/high bits in protected tiers, and train models with the measured 1-to-0 decay statistics so old entries gracefully lose precision (8b toward 4b) as they age, matching how attention importance decays.
why: Refresh zero for ~half of AI working capacity; accuracy loss targeted <0.5% through decay-aware training.

title: Retention-tail sparing at word granularity in the base die
idea: Po: the weak cells simply don't exist. After stacking, measure every 64-bit word's retention at 95 C over repeated passes, remap the worst ~0.1% (the fA tail plus variable-retention words) to a spare tier through a CAM in the logic base die, so every remaining word retains >10 s and refresh is disabled for shorter-lived data.
why: Refresh: repairs the tail (fact 3) instead of refreshing for it; one spare tier per 32 is cheap in 3D. Variable retention time is the main risk.

title: Graphene-hBN barristor access with a tunnelling-barrier off state
idea: Po: the switch is a wall electrons cannot climb. Build a vertical access device of graphene, 3-5 layers of hBN and MoS2 where the wordline tunes the graphene Fermi level and thus the barrier height to the storage node; the off state needs emission over ~1 eV plus tunnelling through hBN (<1e-21 A), and devices stack as van der Waals tiers.
why: Refresh eliminated at ~4F2 vertical footprint; risks are wafer-scale vdW growth or transfer and on-current.

title: Laser-seeded single-grain channels erase the leakage tail
idea: Po: every transistor is carved from a perfect crystal. In each 3D tier, crystallize the access channel from amorphous Si by location-controlled excimer-laser growth from a seed hole (micro-Czochralski) so every channel is one grain; grain-boundary trap-assisted tunnelling, the main source of the fA tail in polycrystalline tiers, disappears.
why: Refresh: tail collapses toward the median (>10 s at 85 C) so refresh can be disabled for lifetime-bounded data; also tightens tier-to-tier Vt (fact 2).
